newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sentrachem announces major restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Sentrachem announces major restructuring.

text.p: South African chemicals group Sentrachem Ltd said on Tuesday it had approved a restructuring and repositioning programme to give the group greater focus and efficiency.

Managing director John Job said in a statement that the action followed a detailed review of all the group's activities and should achieve savings in operational expenditure and position the group for the future.
Restructure proposals include the merger of units NCP and Karbochem into a larger and focused industrial chemical company.
Some of these divisions' activities would be relocated elsewhere in the group, while several secondary operations would be disposed of. These moves should result in signficant cost savings, Job said.
Steps towards the restoration of unit Sanachem will continue with plans to remove between 300 million and 350 million rand in working capital costs, and the elimination of other costs.

These moves follow a disastrous first half-year for Sentrachem in which one-off charges of 261 million rand due to forward cover contracts and restructuring costs at its Sanachem unit, plunged the group into a loss.
Sentrachem also said that it planned to reduce group debt by about one billion rand over the next 12 to 18 months.

At the same time a study had been undertaken to establish the feasibility of listing an international speciality chemicals business, anchored around Hampshire Chemical Corp, on the New York or London Stock Exchange.

Other parts of the restructure programme include the continuation of a partnership between Sentrachem and Hoechst South Africa Ltd. However, to ensure that their polyolefins business is positioned correctly both will probe the optimal structure of the Safripol/Platomark venture.

Sentrachem said a new company Syntheta (Pty) Ltd will be formed to include Delta G and the group's fine chemicals activities, focusing on pharmaceuticals and agricultural science products. The need to consolidate these activities had been under investigation for some time, the firm said.
The restructure programme is subject to the listing requirements of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange as well as other necessary regulatory and shareholder approvals.
Job said Sentrachem would make further announcements on the progress of implementing the proposals.
